newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq again appeals for faster food deliveries.
newsitem.headline: Iraq again appeals for faster food deliveries.

text.p: Iraq appealed to non-aligned members of the Security Council on Tuesday to support its demand for speedier delivery of food and other supplies as part of an "oil-for-food" deal.
Iraqi U.N. envoy Nizar Hamdoon, who took the same message on Monday to Secretary-General Kofi Annan, made the appeal in a meeting with members of the council's non-aligned caucus.

The "oil-for-food" agreement, which took effect Dec. 10, permits Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other necessities to offset the effects of sanctions imposed after Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Hamdoon said Monday that, two months after the agreement became operative, no humanitarian goods had yet arrived in Iraq. He said the process of getting contracts approved by the U.N. Iraqi sanctions committee was "very cumbersome and time-consuming."
On Tuesday, he said the committee had so for approved only four of the 10 contracts submitted to it and that Iraq had received no explanation why some were being delayed.
He also said another 80 contracts for various purchases by Iraq were still somewhere in the U.N. secretariat and had not yet reached the sanctions committee.
Asked Monday about contracts for the sale of Iraqi oil, which have to be approved by U.N. overseers, he said: "We have not really encountered any difficulties."
